name: Tarsons Products Ltd
title: Tarsons Products Ltd - 543399 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Capex cycle ending: FY27 depreciation peaks at INR105-110 crores and maintenance capex ~INR20 crores, but Q4 standalone export fell 13.4% and gross margin slipped to ~58.5% on raw-material spikes.

summary.headline: Tarsons Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 7.3% to INR120.9 crore, but margins compressed on raw material spikes and new-plant costs; FY27 PAT guided moderate.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with standalone revenue up 4.4% YoY to about INR97 crore and domestic growth of 11.7% offsetting a 13.4% decline in exports tied to Middle East disruptions. Gross margin fell to 58.5% standalone in Q4 as raw material prices spiked from mid-March, and EBITDA was pressured by commissioning costs at the Amta and Panchla plants. Management said the large capex programme is nearly complete, with full commissioning expected in H1 FY27, and that no major new capex is planned beyond about INR20 crore of maintenance spend. Management guided FY27 PAT to remain at a moderate level, with operating leverage expected to improve from FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Hit by higher depreciation and interest

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated adjusted cash PAT Q4 FY26 / FY26
financial_highlights.change: +9.3% YoY in Q4; +21.4% YoY in FY26

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated cash flow from operations FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR87 crore (INR49 crore from Panchla and Amta)

segments.name: Domestic (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 11.7-12% YoY; FY26 domestic growth was about 7%. Management expects good, stable domestic growth over the next 2-3 years.

segments.name: Exports (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 exports fell 13.4% YoY on Middle East supply-chain disruption, container shortages and freight costs; FY26 exports grew about 3%. Management said some supply-chain easing was seen in the last two weeks and enquiries are reviving.

segments.name: Cell culture / bioprocess
segments.commentary: Bioprocess bottles ramping well; several cell culture lines commercially launched over the last 2-3 months, with pilot production on some lines and more starting in the next quarter. Management expects meaningful scale-up from FY28.

guidance_outlook: Entire capex programme expected to be fully commissioned in H1 FY27.
Standalone depreciation for FY27 guided at about INR105-110 crore, the peak level, as INR158 crore of CWIP moves into fixed assets.
No major capex planned for FY27-28; maintenance and small commercial capex of about INR20 crore in FY27.
FY27 PAT expected at a relatively moderate level, with accounting losses not expected; PAT guided to single-digit percentage with PBT of about 9-10%.
Q1 FY27 gross margin should not fall below 65%, per the CFO, and management said Q1 margins should be in a similar region to Q4.
Net debt target: debt not to exceed 2x EBITDA; free cash flow to be used mainly for deleveraging over the next 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Large-scale capex programme begun about four years ago is in its final phase; bioprocess lines, liquid handling capacity and selected cell culture lines already commissioned.
INR158 crore of CWIP still on the balance sheet, to be capitalised in FY27 and adding depreciation.
Amta and Panchla facilities carried high commissioning and operating costs in FY26 that management expects to stabilise as utilisation ramps up.
Management expects cell culture volumes to be driven by about 10-20 large customers, mix of domestic and international, with significant scale-up from FY28 and stable growth by year 4-5.
Management said it expects to serve Nerbe (consolidated subsidiary) with products from India after capacity expansion, where financially viable.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices rose about 60-70% from normalised levels since mid-March, driven by Middle East and Asian supply disruption; raw material supply is also constrained across the industry.
Management began gradual, product-by-product price increases from April FY27 but said full pass-through is not feasible given price-list cycles and competition from imports and MNC inventory.
Chinese competition in the US and Europe described as fierce; India-EU FTA, if effective, could provide a few percentage points of duty advantage versus China.
Management says exports face US buyer pressure on pricing and that the rupee depreciation is a cost advantage only on local components, with raw materials still imported.
Industry domestic demand declined about 8% YoY while Tarsons grew 4.5% YoY; Q4 Tarsons grew about 16% QoQ versus industry 3%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the depreciation outlook and capex for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation is on written-down value (18% machinery and moulds, 10% buildings). Standalone FY27 depreciation is guided at INR105-110 crore, with no major capex beyond about INR20 crore maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Will export growth be strong in FY27 now that US tariffs have eased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit; raw material spikes have made Indian producers less competitive versus US manufacturers, and stronger growth needs normalised conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q1 FY27 margins be worse than Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 margins should be in a similar range to Q4, not worse; the CFO said gross margin should not fall below 65%, against about 68% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will free cash flow go to deleveraging?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; the focus over 2-3 years is deleveraging, with debt ideally kept below 2x EBITDA. Fundraising could be considered only if a significant opportunity arises.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pass through the full raw material increase to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited price-book cycles (generally annual), competitors absorbing short-term price spikes, and large existing import inventory that could enable price undercutting.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from raw material costs, with management only partially passing through increases and Q1 FY27 margin trajectory uncertain.
Export recovery depends on the Middle East situation, freight and container availability, and US and Europe competition from China.
New capacity (Amta, Panchla, cell culture) ramp-up speed and commissioning costs; cell culture scale-up is not expected until FY28.
Higher depreciation (INR105-110 crore FY27) and interest keep PAT thin, with FY27 PAT guided to moderate levels.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term growth and domestic market share gains but cautious and evasive on near-term export growth, pricing and margins. Several answers deferred to geopolitical and raw material uncertainty, and the call showed some tension with analysts on competitive dynamics.
key_quotes: Tarsons has achieved its highest ever quarterly revenue in Q4 FY'26.
We expect the entire capex program to be fully commissioned during the first half of the current financial year.
We would definitely it would be to deleverage, reduce the debt on our books and I would ideally in a situation -- in an ideal situation, not want debt to increase more than 2x our EBITDA.

adds.what: Amta and Panchla plants (large-scale capex programme, bioprocess lines, liquid handling capacity, selected cell culture lines) - INR158 crore CWIP to be capital

growth.why: Management guided FY27 PAT to a moderate level (PBT ~9-10%, single-digit PAT margin) with no revenue growth number given; INR158 crore CWIP to be capitalised with full commissioning in H1 FY27, and no major new capex beyond ~INR20 crore maintenance, so growth backing is partial and no explicit revenue guidance was stated.
